LESSON: TIME

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Measurement 2.3 Capacity (8 lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, the learner 
Topic 2.4: Time
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Time, part of Measurement 2.3 Capacity (8 lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, the learner  in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: how they look. ● Observe a clock face and discuss the minute and hour hand. How do we read and tell time using digital and analogue clock?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign time and terms related to time,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. relate the months of the year to special occasions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. recite the number of days in each month of the year,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. read the calendar in terms of day and date,

   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. measure time using arbitrary units.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. identify the minute and hour hand in clock face,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

G. read time by the hour from the clock face,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

H. write time by the hour shown by an analogue and digital clock,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

I. appreciate keeping time in day- to-day activities. ● Learners in pairs /groups are guided to identify, fingerspell and sign time and terms related to time, i.e. clock, digital and analog clock, minute, ‘past’, ‘to’. ● In pairs or groups, discuss special occasions that take place in different months of the year. ● In pairs or groups, sign sing songs and rhymes related to the number of days in the months of the year. ● In pairs or groups, discuss how to read, tell and write dates from the calendar. ● In pairs or groups, discuss and relate time by hour using the length of a shadow of an object such as a tree in the environment. ● Discuss places where clocks are displayed and how they look. ● Observe a clock face and discuss the minute and hour hand. How do we read and tell time using digital and analogue clock? 25 ● Discuss how to read, tell and write time by the hour using both the analogue and digital clock. ● Discuss the importance of keeping time in different activities.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Time together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: Signing and observing clearly and effectively as they discuss in pairs or in groups how to tell

time on the clock face using “past” and “to” the hour.

Values:
• Respect: patiently wait for their turn to read and tell time on a digital clock.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Governance: Law and order in school in keeping time as learners in turns read and tell time on a digital clock.

Link to other learning areas:

• Learners relate time skills to positions and direction in Environmental education and activities.

Suggested Learning resources:

● Clock face both analogue and digital, tactile clock face, manilla paper
